description: STUMPY is a powerful and scalable Python library for modern time series analysis

summary.one_liner: STUMPY is a Python library for computing matrix profiles of time series and using them for pattern discovery, anomaly detection, and segmentation, with Numba, Dask, and GPU backends.
summary.what_it_does: STUMPY computes the matrix profile of a time series, which for each subsequence records its nearest-neighbor subsequence elsewhere in the series. The README says the matrix profile can then support motif (approximately repeated subsequence) discovery, discord/anomaly detection, shapelet discovery, semantic segmentation, and streaming updates. It also lists time series chains, snippets, and pan matrix profiles for choosing window sizes. The library provides stump for 1-D series, mstump for multi-dimensional series, and distributed (stumped, mstumped) and GPU (gpu_stump) variants. It also provides anchored time series chains (atsc, allc) and FLUSS segmentation (fluss). The README includes a benchmark table comparing CPU, Dask cluster, and GPU runtimes across series lengths.
use_cases: find repeated patterns in sensor or sales time series
detect anomalies or discords in a time series
segment a time series into regimes
compute matrix profiles on large series with multiple CPUs or a Dask cluster
accelerate matrix profile computation on NVIDIA GPUs
notable: Matrix profile computation for 1-D and multi-dimensional time series
Distributed execution through Dask Distributed (stumped, mstumped)
GPU execution with Numba CUDA (gpu_stump), supporting multiple devices
Includes FLUSS semantic segmentation and anchored time series chains
Benchmarks in README span from 64 points to 134 million points
caveats: Requires Python 3.11 or newer according to the README; not compatible with Python 2.x
GPU and distributed features need CUDA hardware or a Dask cluster, which the README describes but does not detail for setup
Performance table reports results on specific older hardware; runtimes will vary
keywords: detect unusual values in a sensor stream
split a time series into regimes
